blocks.text: The words a Russian grammar, a dictionary or a teacher uses for the things this site teaches — the vocabulary you need to ask a question about Russian in Russian. Each lesson after this page takes a group of them: the term, its English, and a one-line English definition from the dictionary; then which term each definition is of. Review Terms drills the whole list — here, and from the Vocabulary tab.

terms.def: A system of rules and principles for the structure of a language, or of languages in general.
The study of the internal structure of morphemes (words and their semantic building blocks).
The study of the structure of phrases, sentences, and language.
A method of representing a language or the sounds of language by written symbols.
A set of symbols and marks which are used to clarify meaning in text by separating strings of words into clauses, phrases and sentences.
The set of all words and phrases in a language; any unified subset of words from a particular language.
The relative emphasis or prominence given to a certain syllable in a word or to a certain word in a phrase or sentence.
A linguistic category of words sharing syntactic or morphological behaviour and semantic properties, such as noun or verb.
A word that functions as the name of a specific object or set of objects, such as person, animal, place, word, thing, phenomenon, substance, quality, or idea.
A word that indicates an action, event, or state of being.
A word that modifies a verb, adjective, other adverbs, or various other types of words, phrases, or clauses.
A word or a group of words that one may substitute for a noun or noun phrase.
A number word, a simple or compound word for a number often having particular grammatical attributes depending on the language.
Any of a class of non-inflecting words and multiword terms typically employed to connect a following noun or a pronoun, in an adjectival or adverbial sense, with some other word.
A word used to join other words, phrases, or clauses together into sentences.
A part of speech that has no inherent lexical definition but must be associated with another word to impart meaning, often a grammatical category.
A phrase or word with no particular grammatical relation to a sentence but which serves to express emotion or as a filled pause.
A form of a verb that may function as an adjective, noun or adverb.
A participle that modifies a verb in the same sentence and is equivalent to an adverbial clause in English.
A specific inflection of a word (particularly a noun, pronoun, or adjective) depending on its function in the sentence.
The case used to indicate the subject—or agent—of a finite verb.
The grammatical case, chiefly applicable to nouns, used to express a relationship of origin or possession.
Case used to express direction towards an indirect object, the recipient or beneficiary of an action.
The case used to mark the immediate object (direct object) on which the transitive verb acts.
A noun case used to express means or agency.
A noun case serving as object of a preposition.
A way of categorizing nouns, pronouns, or adjectives according to the inflections they receive.
A division of nouns and pronouns (and sometimes of other parts of speech) into masculine or feminine, and sometimes other categories like neuter or common, and animate or inanimate.
Of, pertaining or belonging to the male grammatical gender, in languages that have gender distinctions.
Of, pertaining or belonging to the female grammatical gender, in languages that have gender distinctions.
Having a form which is not masculine nor feminine.
Of a word or phrase, the state of being singular, dual or plural, shown by inflection.
A form of a word that refers to only one person or thing.
A word in the form in which it potentially refers to something other than one person or thing.
The characteristic of a noun, dependent on its living or sentient nature, which affects grammatical features.
The last morpheme of a word, added to some base to make an inflected form (such as -s in "dogs").
The main part of an uninflected word to which affixes may be added to form inflections of the word.
The primary lexical unit of a word, which carries the most significant aspects of semantic content and cannot be reduced into smaller constituents.
A morpheme added to the beginning of a word to modify its meaning.
A morpheme added at the end of a word to modify the word's meaning.
A grammatical category that expresses how a verbal action, event, or state, extends over time.
A grammatical aspect that describes an action viewed as a simple whole.
A grammatical aspect used for ongoing, habitual, repeated, or similar semantic roles, whether they are in the past, present, or future.
The property of indicating the point in time at which an action or state of being occurs or exists.
A grammatical tense whose principal function is to locate a situation or event in the present time.
A grammatical tense whose function is to place an action or situation in the past.
The tense or time form of a verb used to refer to an event or occurrence that has not yet happened or is expected to happen in the future.
A linguistic category used to distinguish between the speaker of an utterance and those to whom or about whom they are speaking.
A verb form that depends on how its containing clause relates to the speaker’s or writer’s wish, intent, or assertion about reality.
The mood of a verb used in ordinary, factual, or objective statements.
The grammatical mood generally expressing a command, though also used to express a request or permission.
Mood expressing an action or state which is hypothetical or anticipated rather than actual, including wishes and commands.
A particular way of inflecting or conjugating verbs, or a particular form of a verb, which indicates the relation of the subject of the verb to the action which the verb expresses.
The form in which the subject of a verb carries out some action.
The form of a transitive verb in which its subject receives the action.
The act or process of conjugating a verb.

A non-finite verb form considered neutral with respect to inflection; depending on language variously found used with auxiliary verbs, in subordinate clauses, or acting as a gerund, and often as the dictionary form.
A verb whose subject and direct object are the same.
A verb that is accompanied (either clearly or implicitly) by a direct object in the active voice.
A word that modifies a noun or noun phrase or describes a noun’s referent.
A form of an adjective that indicates a different degree of the attribute the adjective denotes; like the positive, comparative and superlative forms.
The degree of comparison of an adjective or adverb used when comparing two entities in terms of a certain property or a certain way of doing something.
The degree of comparison of an adjective or adverb used when comparing three or more entities in terms of a certain property or a certain way of doing something.
Particularly in Slavic languages, a shortened form of the adjective, used predicatively.
A grammatically complete series of words consisting of a subject and predicate, even if one or the other is implied.
A word or, more commonly, a group of words that functions as a single unit in the syntax of a sentence.
The noun, pronoun or noun phrase about whom the statement is made.
The part of the sentence (or clause) which states a property that a subject has or is characterized by.
The noun phrase which is an internal complement of a verb phrase or a prepositional phrase. In a verb phrase with a transitive action verb, it is typically the receiver of the action.
A word that qualifies a noun.
A word or a group of words that modifies or more closely defines the sentence or the verb.
A sound produced by the vocal cords with relatively little restriction of the oral cavity, forming the prominent sound of a syllable.
A sound that results from the passage of air through restrictions of the oral cavity.
A unit of human speech which often forms words corresponding to one opening of the mouth; a vowel and its surrounding consonants.
A symbol in an alphabet.
The set of letters used when writing in a language.
The Cyrillic letter Ъ/ъ, which in modern languages serves to denote a hard (non-palatalized) consonant.
The Cyrillic letter Ь/ь, which in modern languages using the Cyrillic alphabet serves to denote a soft (palatized) consonant.
